name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,166

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Caliph in time repelled by superior might

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back the way it came, so this word is read backwards

blocks.note: U is the old abbreviation for upper-class or superior
may and might are forms of the same verb
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A caliph is pushed back in his time by a stronger power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means placed beside: the reversed time sits after the superior might, giving UMAYYAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Umayyads were the dynasty of caliphs ruling from Damascus, so an Umayyad is one such Islamic ruler.

clue.text: Letters from middle of July, one of them placed in Jiffy bag

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two inner letters, so only those are used
placed in puts one letter inside the following word

blocks.note: the two central letters
in a jiffy means in a trice, an instant

explanation.surface: Letters sent in mid-July, one of them stuffed into a padded envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Jiffy bag, a British padded envelope, splits in two: Jiffy is the instant and bag is the definition. U leads, and L, one of the two letters, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A utricle is a small sac or bladder in an animal or plant, such as the one in the inner ear.

clue.text: Will's cow, when worried, falling across reserve milk container

indicators.note: in a down entry, falling means dropping below, so the word before goes underneath the pieces it falls across

blocks.note: as can mean when
a sub is a reserve player
a jug holds milk
ate means gnawed or worried, as something eats at you

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's cow, fretting, keeps falling over the spare milk churn.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is Shakespeare and 'cow' is the verb, to intimidate. ATE comes from 'worried' but falls below the rest in this down entry, which is what 'falling across' tells you.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used assubjugate in Troilus and Cressida to mean subdue or debase, as to cow someone is to subdue them.

clue.text: Raised a question with contrasting responses about Fijian drink

indicators.note: about means around, so the two answers are wrapped around the question
raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
no and ay, the opposite answers
Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question about a Fiji drink and gets yes and no for answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ay is an old or dialect yes, so NO and AY are the contrasting answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaqona is the Fijian name for kava, the ceremonial drink made from the root of a pepper plant.

clue.text: National radio host with one engagement in surrounding area

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the preceding word goes around the following one

blocks.note: a disc jockey hosts a radio show
Roman numeral one
a bout is a fight or engagement
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A national radio presenter has a booking in the surrounding region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective for the radio station, but it is a noun: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Djiboutian is a citizen of Djibouti in the Horn of Africa, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Spiritual leader from time unknown put on a measure of intelligence

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
to put on is to add
intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: A guru's sayings, handed down from time immemorial, raised everyone's intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: TZADDIQ is a Hebrew word, also spelt tsaddik; the Z from algebra's unknowns is what makes the odd spelling gettable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tzaddiq is a righteous man, specifically the revered rebbe who heads a Hasidic Jewish community.

clue.text: Punishment the aim of boxer with big punch?

blocks.note: purpose is expressed with to, as in in order to
a knockout, what a heavy puncher delivers

explanation.surface: The point of a hard-hitting boxer is to punish his opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful reading: a big puncher aims to KO, to knock out.
explanation.definitionFit: Toko is Anglo-Indian and dialect slang for a thrashing or chastisement, so it means a beating or penalty.

clue.text: Girl made trip — panned after forgetting cases

indicators.note: a word's case is its outside, its first and last letters; forgetting them leaves only the inside of each word

blocks.note: the inner letters
the inner letters
the inner letters

explanation.surface: A girl set off on a journey that the critics slammed, after losing her suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgetting cases' applies to all three words before it: each loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrianne is a woman's given name, a variant of Adrienne, so the answer is a girl's name.

clue.text: Rabbit, perhaps, ready to be caught by the ears

indicators.text: to be caught by the ears
indicators.note: something caught by the ears is heard rather than seen, so go by sound

blocks.note: ready is slang for cash, as is dough

explanation.surface: A rabbit is lifted by its ears, ready to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready, short for ready money, is British slang for cash; dough is the same slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rabbit is called a doe, as are the females of deer and hares; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: As monarch heads for exit, nobody looks for resistance in dispute

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters, so each of the next three words gives only its first
for here means in place of: these letters stand where the other letter was

blocks.note: to query something is to dispute it
initial letters
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: As the king heads out, no one is looking for opposition in the quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Queenly means befitting a queen, so it describes behaving as a monarch would, regal in manner.

clue.text: Cape or long cloth garment cut back

indicators.note: a garment that is cut loses its end, so drop the final letter
back tells you to read what remains from right to left

blocks.note: the sari is a long draped cloth worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: A tailor asks whether to shorten a cape or a long robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras is an Arabic word for a headland, found in many place names, so it is a promontory or cape.

clue.text: Cake regularly available in grill — ultimately bizarre way to keep food

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a verb answer: the process named by the verb

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter of the word before it
in puts the preceding letters inside the next word
ultimately points to the very end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: to grill someone is to question or quiz them
first and third letters
free means available
the final letter

explanation.surface: Cake that's on offer at the grill: an odd way to store food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' and 'grill' set up a kitchen, but grill means to question closely, and the cake only lends two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To quick-freeze is to freeze food rapidly so it keeps its texture, a standard method of preservation.

clue.text: Young attendant excited by a coin — tip from Arab

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and thrown into a new order
a tip is an end point, here the far end of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
the tip at the end of the word

explanation.surface: A young servant thrilled to be handed a coin as a tip by an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link joining 'excited' to the coin, but it is part of the letters being mixed, and the tip is the last letter of Arab, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin boy is a boy employed to wait on a ship's officers and passengers, a young servant at sea.

clue.text: Judge one visiting land a foreigner

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so these letters are put inside the next word

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
Roman numeral one
to land a prize is to gain it

explanation.surface: A judge on a visit abroad finds himself the foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge and the one go in as a pair, between the last two letters of the land word rather than at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaijin is the Japanese word for an outsider, a non-Japanese person living in or visiting Japan.

clue.text: Start of March historically ushers in verse on a spring bird

indicators.note: to usher someone in is to bring them inside, so the following letters go within the first word

blocks.note: the 1936 Jarrow March began in this town
V is the abbreviation for verse
taken as written
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Early March, historically, brings poems about a bird in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarrow, a town in north-east England, is where the 1936 Jarrow Crusade hunger march to London set out. 'On' puts V before A SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Java sparrow is a finch native to Java and Bali, kept widely as a cage bird.

clue.text: Pants with large parka are an aid to getting about

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters that follow are in a poor state and need sorting out

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
L is the abbreviation for large
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Trousers paired with a big anorak help you get around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a garment to go with the parka, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A parawalker is a powered orthosis worn by people with paraplegia, letting them stand and walk.

clue.text: Old poet's outlaw to be transported briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to exult is to be carried away with joy

explanation.surface: An ancient poet's tale of a bandit sentenced to transportation for a short term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests convicts shipped to Australia, but here it means overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exul is Spenser's spelling of exile, a person banished, which is how an old poet named an outlaw.

clue.text: Shrewd, going round gang with new, powerful digger

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so this word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: savvy means knowing or shrewd
a gang of workers is a team
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A canny foreman gets round his work gang with a mighty new excavator.
explanation.walkthrough: A navvy is a British word for a labourer digging canals or railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam navvy is a steam-driven mechanical shovel, the excavating machine that replaced gangs of labourers.

clue.text: Fighter pierced by harmful article? Spike?

indicators.note: something pierced has another thing driven into it, so the next word goes inside

blocks.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boxer is stabbed by a dangerous object: was it a spike?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Spike is a first name, not a sharp point.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Milligan was the Irish-born comedian of The Goon Show, so a Spike, by example, is Milligan.

clue.text: Canopy no one put back on fake arch's exterior

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so these letters are read in the opposite direction
the exterior of a word is its outside, so only its two end letters are kept

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
nay is an old word for no
Roman numeral one
first and last letters

explanation.surface: No one restored the canopy over the outside of the imitation arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the reversed piece after SHAM in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamiyanah is an Indian awning or ornamental tent roof, a decorated cloth canopy for gatherings.

clue.text: For seafood platter, six dry gas rings

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the preceding word goes round the numeral

blocks.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine
Roman numeral six
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: For a seafood platter, six dry gas rings are needed in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas rings sound like hob burners, but the rings are the containing instruction and gas is helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Seviche, usually ceviche, is a Latin American dish of raw fish marinated in citrus, served as a plate of seafood.

clue.text: Bones returning in the role of Spock's first love

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name before it is taken
returning means going back the way it came, so the whole string runs right to left

blocks.note: acting as means in the role of
the initial letter
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Bones from Star Trek comes back as Spock's first love interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' is also the nickname of Dr McCoy in Star Trek, which the surface plays on, but here it is plain anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for a bone, so it means several bones.

clue.text: Development of relations, mostly uplifting ones

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
uplifting in a down clue raises the letters, so they read from the bottom up

blocks.note: relations as in sexual relations
the plural of I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Building family ties, most relations prove encouraging people.
explanation.walkthrough: Relations stands for the adjective in the phrase sexual relations, a loose step; trimmed and turned upward it heads the answer, with IS below.
explanation.definitionFit: Auxesis is the technical term for growth by enlargement of cells, and in rhetoric for amplification, both forms of development.

clue.text: Place applied for expanded

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
something applied has been used

explanation.surface: A job applicant whose prospects grew.
explanation.definitionFit: To plus is to increase or add to, so plused means enlarged, a sense used mainly in American English.

clue.text: Jockey cunning, abandoning one in local fair

indicators.note: abandoning one means leaving behind an I, the numeral one, from the word just before

blocks.note: to jockey for position is to vie
wily means cunning

explanation.surface: A crafty jockey drops out of the race at the village fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word, and 'fair' is the adjective for good-looking, not a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewly is a northern English dialect word meaning pleasant to look at, so attractive in a regional sense.

clue.text: Couple flanking VW following ace short story-teller's old tales

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter of the next word goes
following means coming after, so the pair is placed behind the pieces named next

blocks.note: ace and fab are both slang for excellent
a liar tells stories
the two letters on either side of V and W in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A couple either side of a Volkswagen listen to a great short-story writer's old yarns.
explanation.walkthrough: VW looks like the car, but it is just two letters of the alphabet, and the couple flanking them are their neighbours in alphabetical order. Ace as slang for excellent is the same as fab.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabliaux are the comic, often bawdy verse stories of medieval France, so they are old tales.

clue.text: Animal hair left in jam

indicators.note: in puts the letter for the side inside the next word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
to be in a jam is to be in a fix

explanation.surface: Fur from an animal got stuck in the jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Flix is an old word for fur or the down of an animal such as a beaver or hare.

clue.text: Witches, close to evening, ask Lucifer for a new spell

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken
a new spell is a fresh spelling, so the letters are rearranged into a different order

blocks.note: the final letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: As night falls, a coven of witches asks the Devil to grant them a fresh spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The witches are not hags but fish: witch is the name of a flatfish, and 'spell' means spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Craig fluke is another name for the witch, a North Atlantic flatfish related to the flounder.

clue.text: Japanese catch up Guyanese hosts

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so the letters are found within the next word
up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the second to fourth letters

explanation.surface: People in Guyana take in a fish caught in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The ayu, or sweetfish, is a small river fish prized in Japan, often caught by fishing with cormorants.

clue.text: Notes land specially set aside

blocks.note: first meaning: the plural of re, the second note of the sol-fa scale
second meaning: short for reservation, land set aside for a people

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is the North American short form for an Indigenous reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: Res serves both as the plural of the musical note re and as a clipped form of reservation, territory set apart.

clue.text: March happening sometime which Latin number opens

indicators.note: opens means splits apart, so these letters force their way into the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: sometime means former, as ex does
qui is Latin for which or who
NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Something happens in March: but which Latin numeral starts it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sometime' looks like part of the definition, but it is the wordplay's EX, in its sense of former.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring equinox, when day and night are equal, falls around 20 March each year, an annual event of that month.

clue.text: Perform again: did live dances

blocks.note: to redo is to do again
was means existed, did live

explanation.surface: An encore: performers once did live dances.
explanation.definitionFit: The redowa is a Bohemian couple dance, a kind of waltz, so redowas are dances of that type.
